svg.title: The Call Network Flywheel
svg.desc: diagram id: diag-06-network-flywheel-architecture; chapter number: 11; chart type: org_architecture; title: The Call Network Flywheel; subtitle: Buyer coverage attracts publishers; owned tracking holds the margin; caption: Start as an affiliate sending calls into networks, load-balance across several, then go direct to buyers, because a network-to-direct jump is worth 100 to 300 points.; assumptions note: Network margins of 35-100% on average and 100-400% observed are Ringba masterclass figures; 8-12 applications for 4-6 acceptances is Ryan Moran's estimate. Team size is not quoted by practitioners.; note: Sources: Ringba (20s5iGyl_MY, RhODbxB4ylU, AMwEMCOuhA0, Jvd7AeYwbns), ExclusiveLiveCall (Cu3vdN7Cn84), Ryan Moran (NC4s18S7p00).; center: role: Call broker owning tracking and routing; headcount: Not quoted by practitioners; focus: Lock payout bumps in writing and never bluff a takeaway; spokes: role: Affiliate networks; type: Entry lane and load balancing; kpi: 8-12 applications for 4-6 acceptances; a guaranteed concurrency figure; role: Direct local buyers; type: Demand; kpi: 10 to 20-plus buyers per market; a $10 network call becomes $30-$80 direct; role: Publishers; type: Supply; kpi: Separate sub IDs, conservative caps, paid on time after call review; role: Call tracking platform; type: Control layer; kpi: Duplicate calls routed to different networks get paid twice for one caller
